brief.headline: The aluminium price fell and the aluminium curve tightened on the same session - cash off 0.17% to $3,255.50 while the cash-to-three-month spread flipped through flat into a $2.00 backwardation, its first inversion in twelve publishing sessions - and separately the pending Q4 Japanese premium round finally became public, with producers opening 18-22% below the current record.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. Aluminium cash settled $3,255.50 on 02-September, down $5.50 or -0.17%; the three-month settled $3,253.50, down $7.50 or -0.23%. Because the forward fell FURTHER than the prompt, the curve went through flat and into a $2.00 BACKWARDATION - cash above three-month - having been in contango or flat for twelve consecutive sessions. Warehouse stock fell 500 tonnes to 246,225 t, which is more movement than the previous thirteen sessions combined and is still only 0.20% of the total. On the same board nickel cash rose 1.10%, copper fell 0.28%, lead fell 0.05% and zinc fell 2.80%.

WHY IT MOVED, AND WHY THE TWO HALVES OF THE SESSION HAVE DIFFERENT EXPLANATIONS. The flat-price decline needs no fundamental explanation at all: the dollar index rose 0.18%, and for a dollar-denominated commodity that accounts for essentially the whole of a 0.17% decline. The curve move is the part that carries information, because a spread is quoted in dollars on both legs and is therefore currency-neutral. Prompt outperforming forward on a down day says somebody still wants metal now rather than in three months - and it follows a session in which the prompt outperformed the forward by $19.00 on the way up. Two sessions, opposite directions in the flat price, the same direction in the spread, for a cumulative $21.00 of front-end tightening.

WHY TO KEEP THE ENTHUSIASM PROPORTIONATE, WHICH IS THE PART A CURVE HEADLINE HIDES. A $2.00 backwardation on a $3,255.50 metal is SIX BASIS POINTS, and the market printed the same $2.00 inversion on 14-August before spending twelve sessions back in contango - so this is not the first backwardation of the cycle and is not being described as one. A 500-tonne inventory draw is roughly two hours of world primary output. Against those two small positives sit two dated negatives from the same 24 hours: Q4 Japanese premium offers opened at $310-325 against a $395 benchmark, and SMM's alumina read describes strong supply, weak demand, port inventories at historical highs and further downside room.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT. First, whether the backwardation WIDENS or closes over the next few sessions - a persistent and widening inversion alongside a resumed stock draw would be the first genuinely coherent tightness evidence of this cycle, while a snap back into contango marks today as noise. Second, US non-farm payrolls on 04-September, the highest-weight input into a Federal Reserve decision on 16-September that money markets price at roughly 70% for a HIKE; with a hike already the majority-priced outcome the asymmetry sits with a soft print. Third, the Q4 Japanese premium negotiation, now public and running through later in September, with producers at $310-325 and buyers targeting below $300.

lme.commentary: THE 02-SEPTEMBER SESSION SHOULD BE READ AS TWO SEPARATE EVENTS WITH TWO SEPARATE EXPLANATIONS, AND CONFLATING THEM IS THE MAIN WAY TO GET TODAY WRONG. EVENT ONE IS THE FLAT PRICE AND IT IS UNINTERESTING: cash $3,255.50 down $5.50 or -0.17%, three-month $3,253.50 down $7.50 or -0.23%, on a session when the dollar index rose 0.18%. For a dollar-denominated commodity that currency move accounts for essentially the whole decline, and in euro terms the same settlement fell roughly 0.04% rather than 0.17%. NO FUNDAMENTAL INPUT IS REQUIRED TO EXPLAIN EVENT ONE, and the more parsimonious reading is the correct one. EVENT TWO IS THE CURVE AND IT IS THE REASON THIS COMMENTARY EXISTS: the spread went through flat into a $2.00 BACKWARDATION - cash above three-month - for the first time in twelve publishing sessions. A SPREAD IS CURRENCY-NEUTRAL BECAUSE BOTH LEGS ARE QUOTED IN DOLLARS, so the dollar explanation that disposes of event one does not touch event two. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THIS PAGE FLAGS THAT COMBINATION EXPLICITLY EVERY TIME IT OCCURS. Price down with the prompt tightening means the macro won the session while somebody still wanted metal now rather than in three months. THE TWO-SESSION SEQUENCE IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN EITHER SESSION: on 01-September the prompt outperformed the forward by $19.00 inside a rally; on 02-September it outperformed by $2.00 inside a decline; cumulative front-end tightening of $21.00 across two sessions that went opposite ways in the flat price. A signal that survives a direction change in the underlying is worth more than one that does not. NOW THE DISCIPLINE, BECAUSE THIS PAGE WILL NOT OVERSELL A SIX-BASIS-POINT NUMBER. A $2.00 backwardation on a $3,255.50 metal is 0.06%. THE BOARD PRINTED EXACTLY THIS +$2.00 INVERSION ON 14-AUGUST, AND +$4.00 ON 13-AUGUST, AND THEN SPENT TWELVE CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS BACK IN CONTANGO - so any claim that this is the first backwardation of the cycle is false and is not made here. The completed August average spread was a $1.60 CONTANGO, which is the useful benchmark: today sits on the opposite side of the month's own mean, which is a change of state, but a small one that has reversed before. THE INVENTORY LINE GAVE ITS FIRST CORROBORATION OF THE CYCLE AND IT IS EQUALLY SMALL. Stock fell 500 t to 246,225 t after printing 246,725 t for three consecutive sessions and moving 200 t across thirteen. Today's move exceeds the previous thirteen sessions combined and is still 0.20% of the total, roughly two hours of world primary output. FOR SCALE, LEAD - WITH NO SUPPLY STORY AT ALL - DREW 5,075 TONNES ON THE SAME BOARD, TEN TIMES AS MUCH. What makes the aluminium draw worth reporting is not its size but its coincidence: it is the first session in this cycle on which the curve and the inventory pointed the same way at the same time. THE CROSS-METAL EVIDENCE IS THE STRONGEST PART OF TODAY AND IT POINTS TO SOMETHING METAL-SPECIFIC. Four curves moved in four different directions on one board: aluminium's tightened $2.00 through flat into inversion; copper's backwardation NARROWED $52.50 from $180.50 to $128.00; nickel's contango COLLAPSED $180.00 from $325.00 to $145.00 on an unchanged forward; zinc's backwardation compressed $55.00. A common funding or risk-appetite shift moves every curve the same way. These did not, which is evidence against a shared factor and in favour of position-specific flows. THE HONEST CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED FROM YESTERDAY IN SUBSTANCE AND SHARPER IN DETAIL: aluminium is being bid at the front for a reason the other metals do not share, and the reason is almost certainly Gulf supply - Gulf primary output was down 44% year on year in July and further tanker attacks were reported overnight. But the flat price gave back part of yesterday's move while that story was unchanged, which is what a positioning premium does and not what a shortage does. Until the backwardation widens AND persists AND the stock draw continues at a scale larger than two hours of output, this remains a risk premium being re-paid rather than a physical shortage arriving.

The pending quarter is handled separately in the settlement-history panel, with a null value and a scenario range. THE COMMERCIAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THE OFFER RANGE IS NEVERTHELESS LARGE AND IS STATED HERE: producers opening at $310-325 against a $395 benchmark is a producer-side acknowledgement that the Q3 record was a peak, and Reuters reports the Japanese buy side is targeting BELOW $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian shipments. A source at a Japanese rolling mill is quoted saying the opening offers were closer to realistic levels than in the previous round but still too high given weak spot prices. A record-low port stock and a 44% Gulf shortfall are not the conditions in which a buy side normally wins a sub-$300 print.

drivers.text: Q4-2026 producer offers are public and 18-22% below the Q3 record — Top global producers, including Rio Tinto and South32, have offered Japanese buyers $310-$325/t for October-December primary shipments against the Q3-2026 benchmark of $395/t. Reuters attributes the cut to two stated causes: a positive progress report on Middle East production restarts, and softer premiums in Europe. Buyers are pushing for below $300. This is the first hard public number on the pending quarter and it replaces the wider judgement-based range this page previously carried.
drivers.source: Reuters via MINING.COM - Aluminium producers offer Japanese buyers lower Q4 premiums, 02-Sep-2026

drivers.text: Japanese port inventory is at its lowest since April 2010, which cuts against the offer direction — Aluminium stocks at Japan's three major ports fell to 201,000 tonnes at end-July, the lowest since April 2010, per Marubeni. A buy side negotiating a 20% premium cut while sitting on a sixteen-year inventory low is negotiating from a weaker physical position than the headline offer cut implies. Reuters also cites a producer source noting that Iran-war shipment-disruption concerns and strong Japanese semiconductor-related demand continue to support the market.
drivers.source: Reuters via MINING.COM - Aluminium producers offer Japanese buyers lower Q4 premiums, 02-Sep-2026

drivers.text: Gulf primary output was down 44% year on year in July and that is the supply fact underneath every Asian premium — Global primary aluminium output fell 1.7% year on year in July, with GULF PRODUCTION DOWN 44%, per the International Aluminium Institute. Two Gulf smelters accounting for roughly 9% of world primary capacity came under attack in March and were also prevented from shipping through their normal export channels. The premium consequence is delivered-cost, not flat-price: metal that cannot leave the Gulf on its usual route has to be replaced from further away, and that distance is priced in the regional premium rather than on the LME.
drivers.source: Reuters via MINING.COM - Aluminium producers offer Japanese buyers lower Q4 premiums, 02-Sep-2026

drivers.text: US Section 232 is verified at 50% and now carries an investment-linked half-rate carve-out — The rate is re-verified this run: 50% on aluminium articles and Annex I-A derivatives, 25% on Annex I-B derivatives, effective 08-June-2026, plus a 15% transitional rate for metal-intensive industrial and electrical-grid equipment through 31-December-2027. A Section 232 incentive programme effective 20-July-2026 additionally allows approved companies investing in US primary aluminium capacity to import primary metal tied to expected output at HALF the applicable rate. At the 02-September cash official of $3,255.50 the headline tariff leg is $1,627.75/t, or 77.7% of the $2,094/t US Midwest duty-paid premium. NO FREIGHT, FINANCING OR TIGHTNESS SPLIT IS ASSERTED FOR THE REMAINING 22.3% because no public decomposition exists.

logistics.note: THIS ROW IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND THAT IS ITSELF THE NEWS, BECAUSE THE MARKET STEPPED BACK FROM IT ON THE SAME DAY. Public reporting on 01/02-September describes further tanker attacks in the Strait, including an Iranian strike on a Saudi tanker reported by the BBC to have killed two Filipino sailors, following the two tankers struck on Monday night per the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre. Publicly maintained transit trackers put commercial movement at a small fraction of the roughly 85 vessels a day that is normal. THE CRITICAL DISCIPLINE ON THIS ROW IS THAT THE PUBLIC SOURCES DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER AND THIS PAGE DOES NOT PICK A WINNER: activist and open-source trackers describe the corridor as effectively closed, while the US Treasury Secretary stated on the record that 17 million barrels of crude crossed on Monday, which is not the throughput of a closed strait. Both are dated and both are public; they are irreconcilable and are presented as such. WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE is that roughly 9% of world primary aluminium supply exits through this waterway and that Gulf primary output was DOWN 44% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY per the International Aluminium Institute. TODAY'S COMMERCIAL LESSON IS ABOUT DURABILITY RATHER THAN SEVERITY: aluminium led the LME board on 01-September on this story and gave part of it back on 02-September with the story unchanged. A risk premium that decays without the risk decaying is a positioning phenomenon, and positioning unwinds faster than shortages do.

Suez transits remain far below pre-crisis normal and carriers are still routing via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. THE DIRECTION FLAG IS DOWN BECAUSE THE CORRIDOR IS DEGRADED, NOT BECAUSE COSTS ARE FALLING - the two Middle East chokepoints on this page are now both impaired simultaneously, Hormuz by live hostilities and Bab el Mandeb by a blockade with a dated advisory attached, and a producer routing Gulf or Red Sea metal to Europe has no unimpaired option. Sources: https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2026-006-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-gulf-aden-arabian-sea-and-somali-basin-houthi-attacks ; https://gcaptain.com/suez-canal-traffic-stalls-at-60-below-normal-despite-100-days-without-houthi-attacks/

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: STILL NO PUBLIC REPRICE, AND THE ABSENCE IS NOW OLD ENOUGH TO BE A FINDING RATHER THAN A GAP. The last public mark this page can cite is 7.5-10% of hull value from 22-July, against a 1-3% pre-conflict norm. Since that mark, at least four merchant vessels have been reported struck in or near the Strait, including two on Monday night and further attacks reported on 01/02-September. HULL-VALUE PREMIUM IS THE FIRST THING THAT REPRICES AFTER TANKERS ARE PHYSICALLY HIT, so the 22-July figure should be treated as a FLOOR and explicitly not as a current quote. This page will not estimate the current level because war-risk rates are negotiated bilaterally and no public assessment exists. THE COMMERCIAL POINT STANDS WITHOUT THE NUMBER: war-risk cost sits inside every regional premium on this page simultaneously and is completely invisible in the LME flat price, which is one reason a falling LME and firm premiums are not the contradiction they appear to be.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: CARRIED UNCHANGED AT THE 01-SEPTEMBER CLOSE OF 3,157, DOWN 0.91%, BECAUSE NO NEWER FREE DATED PUBLIC PRINT WAS RETRIEVABLE THIS MORNING - the index is stated at its own last public mark rather than rolled to today's date. THE 01-SEPTEMBER SESSION HALTED SEVEN CONSECUTIVE GAINS that had taken the index to 3,186 on 28-August, its highest since 02-June, up 21.05% on the month and 57.33% on the year, Capesize-led. CAPESIZE LEADERSHIP IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR THIS PAGE because Capesize is the ore-and-bauxite end of dry bulk, and SMM names imported bauxite CIF as the driver behind rising Chinese alumina production costs. Freight remains the largest single input-cost inflation in the basket by a wide margin, and unlike the carbon chain it is not offset by anything: a smelter cannot substitute away from the distance between a bauxite mine and a refinery.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: CARRIED AT ITS 20-AUGUST MARK; no newer public composite print was retrievable this run. Container freight matters less for primary ingot, which moves in bulk and breakbulk, and more for VALUE-ADDED and downstream flows - extrusions, rolled coil, foil, finished components - where a rising box rate is a direct margin cost to fabricators rather than to smelters. It is carried as the downstream half of the freight picture, and it is moving the same way as the dry-bulk half.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: GENERIC COMMERCIAL NOTE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN - BUT WITH A NEW FORWARD-LOOKING POINT WORTH FLAGGING GENERICALLY. Contracts written across the Gulf disruption commonly carry force-majeure, war-risk cost-pass-through and demurrage clauses that were drafted for a CLOSED strait. A partial, temporary, 30-to-60-day corridor arrangement of the kind announced on 26-August sits awkwardly between 'closed' and 'open' and is exactly the situation in which such clauses become contested rather than automatic. Anyone with live tonnage under those terms should expect the interpretation question to arrive before the logistics question resolves. This is a general market observation about contract structure and carries no company-specific or confidential content.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: BRENT $95.117, UP 0.49% ON THE DAY AND A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE RISING SESSION, HOLDING ABOVE $95. Crude is the cleanest live proxy this page has for the Hormuz risk premium, because there is no traded instrument that prices aluminium's chokepoint exposure directly. THE SIGNAL TO TAKE FROM IT TODAY IS THAT THE RISK PREMIUM DID NOT UNWIND: oil held its gains on the session in which aluminium gave back a fraction of its own, which argues the Gulf story is still being paid for in the energy complex even though the metal stepped back. The second-order transmission runs through smelter power and alumina refining rather than through sentiment - LNG supply out of the Middle East is the input that took Qatalum to roughly 60% of nameplate and forced Alunorte to 50% for two days in August.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: TTF EUR 74.38/MWh, UP 3.00% - THE LARGEST SINGLE MOVE ANYWHERE ON THIS MACRO PANEL AND THE MOST DIRECTLY RELEVANT ONE TO A SMELTER COST CURVE. Trading Economics headlined European gas climbing to a 2023 high on Strait-related supply news, with UK gas doing the same. EUROPEAN SMELTING IS THE MARGINAL HIGH-COST TONNE IN THE WESTERN SYSTEM and its power contracts are gas-indexed, so a TTF at multi-year highs is simultaneously a cost input and a curtailment risk. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE SUPPLY-RELIEF NARRATIVE THAT DOMINATES THE RISK PANEL: the restart pipeline this page tracks - Slovalco, Magnitude 7's Marston, San Ciprian, Mt Holly - is concentrated in exactly the power-price-sensitive geographies that a gas spike hurts most.

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: DXY 99.859, UP 0.18% - A SECOND CONSECUTIVE FIRMER SESSION AND A MECHANICAL HEADWIND FOR A DOLLAR-DENOMINATED PRICE THAT REQUIRES NO VIEW ABOUT ALUMINIUM AT ALL. Roughly a fifth of a per cent of dollar strength is, other things equal, roughly a fifth of a per cent off the metal - which is most of the 0.17% the cash price actually lost. STATED PLAINLY: TODAY'S ALUMINIUM DECLINE IS FULLY EXPLAINED BY THE CURRENCY WITHOUT NEEDING A SINGLE FUNDAMENTAL INPUT, and that is the more parsimonious reading of a $5.50 move. It is also why the curve, which is currency-neutral because both legs are quoted in dollars, is the more informative half of today's board.

row.note: EUR/USD 1.15681 ON THE LIVE MARKET, DOWN 0.21%. THE OFFICIAL FIXINGS ON THE 02-SEPTEMBER LME BOARD, WHICH ARE THE ONES THAT MATTER FOR ANY EURO-DENOMINATED CONTRACT SETTLING OFF THAT BOARD, MOVED THE SAME WAY: the LME MTLE fixing printed 1.15780 against 1.15930 on 01-September and the ECB 14:15 fixing printed 1.15780 against 1.15900, both a 0.13% stronger dollar between the two sessions. WITH THE CURRENCY STILL, THE DIVERGENCE IS REAL RATHER THAN AN FX ARTEFACT: SHFE aluminium 2610 closed UP RMB 30 or +0.12% at RMB 24,100/t on 02-September while the LME cash official fell 0.17% and the three-month fell 0.23%. SMM attributes the Chinese resilience to continued ingot destocking and the September peak season against hawkish Federal Reserve expectations, and separately notes that the SHFE/LME ratio recovering is expected to weaken Chinese export demand as orders on hand are digested - which is a bearish second-order consequence of the same divergence.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: US 10-YEAR 4.817%, UP 2 BASIS POINTS, AND THE GLOBAL BOND MARKET REMAINS THE LARGEST SINGLE BEARISH FORCE ACTING ON THIS PAGE. The full board is at or near multi-year highs: UK 5.283%, the 10-year JGB THROUGH 3% at 3.018%, Australia 5.225%, GERMANY 3.3884% AND FLAGGED BY TRADING ECONOMICS AS A FRESH 15-YEAR HIGH, France 4.274%, Italy 4.247%. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE TODAY THAN IT DID YESTERDAY, AND IT IS A SPECIFIC MECHANICAL POINT RATHER THAN A MOOD: the aluminium curve has just inverted into a $2.00 backwardation, and a backwardation means holders are PAID to lend metal to the prompt rather than paying to carry it. Rising funding costs and a backwardated curve push in the same direction - both discourage storage and encourage delivery into the front. A $2.00 backwardation against a 4.8% funding rate is nowhere near enough to compensate a carry, so the rational response to today's board is to release metal, not to hoard it. THE SCHEDULED RISK IS 16-SEPTEMBER, with money markets pricing roughly a 70% probability of a 25-basis-point US rate HIKE after the Federal Reserve chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut.

headlines.title: THE CURVE INVERTED INTO BACKWARDATION ON A DAY THE PRICE FELL - cash $3,255.50 settled $2.00 ABOVE the $3,253.50 three-month, the first inversion in twelve publishing sessions, because the forward fell $7.50 while the prompt fell only $5.50. Price DOWN and prompt TIGHTENING is the most information-dense combination a base-metal curve produces, and it is flagged explicitly here. Across two sessions the prompt has now outperformed the forward by a cumulative $21.00, once through a rally and once through a decline, which is a more durable tightening signal than either session alone. THE PROPORTION IS STATED HONESTLY: $2.00 on $3,255.50 is six basis points, and the same $2.00 inversion printed on 14-August before twelve sessions of contango followed.

ALUMINIUM'S ONE-SESSION LEADERSHIP DID NOT REPEAT - after leading the entire LME board on 01-September with a 1.21% cash gain, aluminium finished THIRD OF FIVE on 02-September at -0.17%, behind nickel at +1.10% and lead at -0.05%. The Hormuz story that drove yesterday's move is unchanged and further tanker attacks were reported overnight, so a premium that decayed while its cause persisted is a positioning phenomenon rather than a re-rating. THIS IS THE TEST THIS PAGE SET YESTERDAY AND THE FLAT PRICE FAILED IT; only the curve passed.

Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM OFFERS ARE PUBLIC AT $310-325/t, DOWN 18-22% ON THE RECORD Q3 SETTLEMENT OF $395/t. Reuters, citing four sources in the talks, reports top producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opening at that level, with buyers targeting below $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian shipments. The producers' own stated reasons are supply-relief reasons: positive progress on Middle East restarts and softer European premiums. Talks began the week of 24-August and run through later in September. This page has narrowed its pending-quarter scenario range to $290-325 on the strength of it.

JAPANESE PORT INVENTORY IS AT A SIXTEEN-YEAR LOW AND GULF OUTPUT WAS DOWN 44% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY - aluminium stocks at Japan's three major ports fell to 201,000 tonnes at end-July, the lowest since April 2010 per Marubeni, while global primary output fell 1.7% year on year in July with Gulf production down 44% per the International Aluminium Institute. Two Gulf smelters accounting for roughly 9% of world primary capacity were attacked in March and also lost their normal export channels. A buy side negotiating a 20% premium cut from a sixteen-year inventory low is negotiating from a weaker physical position than the headline offer implies.

SMM'S 02-SEPTEMBER ALUMINA READ IS UNAMBIGUOUSLY BEARISH AND REMOVES THE LAST COST-SIDE SUPPORT UNDER METAL - strong supply against weak demand, domestic Chinese production recovering month on month, Guangxi ramping with new capacity about to be released and Shanxi resuming this month, ex-China prices pulling back as the supply-mismatch logic weakens, PORT INVENTORIES AT HISTORICAL HIGHS and plant inventories rising with output. SMM's own conclusion: supply-side pressure is only increasing, demand shows no bright spots, prices still have downside room. Cheaper alumina is bullish for smelter margins and bearish for metal, because it removes any cost mechanism that could force a curtailment.

SLOVALCO'S SMELTERS ARE FIRING UP AGAIN AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE - AL Circle reported on 02-September that the Slovak plant, curtailed in 2022 on European power costs, has begun restarting. Roughly 75 kt is a tenth of one per cent of world supply and will not move a balance, but it moves a line this page has carried in the 'scheduled' column into the 'happening' column, and it is the same self-correcting pattern that dominates the risk panel: idled Western capacity returns because margins are wide. THE UNRESOLVED TENSION is that a gas-cost casualty is restarting into a European gas market that just printed a multi-year high.

EUROPEAN GAS CLIMBED 3.00% TO A 2023 HIGH ON STRAIT-RELATED SUPPLY NEWS, with UK gas doing the same and Brent up a fourth consecutive session at $95.117. FOR A SMELTER PAGE THIS CUTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE REAL: gas-indexed European power is the marginal high-cost tonne in the Western system, so a TTF spike is simultaneously a cost input, a curtailment risk on the very restarts listed above, and evidence that the Gulf risk premium did NOT unwind in the energy complex even as it decayed in the metal.

THE GLOBAL BOND SELLOFF EXTENDED AND THE GERMAN 10-YEAR HIT A 15-YEAR HIGH - US 10-year 4.817% (+2bp), UK 5.283%, the 10-year JGB through 3% at 3.018%, Australia 5.225%, Germany 3.3884% and flagged as a fresh 15-year high. Money markets price roughly a 70% probability of a 25-basis-point US rate HIKE on 16-September after the Federal Reserve chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut. THE MECHANICAL POINT IS SHARPER TODAY THAN USUAL: with the curve now backwardated, holders are paid to lend metal to the prompt rather than to carry it, and a $2.00 backwardation against a 4.8% funding cost is nowhere near enough to compensate a carry - so rising rates and an inverted curve both point toward releasing metal, not hoarding it.

A FIRMER DOLLAR ACCOUNTS FOR ESSENTIALLY THE WHOLE OF TODAY'S ALUMINIUM DECLINE - DXY 99.859, up 0.18%, with EUR/USD down 0.21% to 1.15681 on the live market and the LME MTLE and ECB fixings both 0.13% stronger dollar between the 01- and 02-September boards. In euro terms the same cash settlement fell roughly 0.04% against 0.17% in dollars. STATED PLAINLY: the flat-price move requires no fundamental explanation at all, which is precisely why the currency-neutral spread is the more informative half of today's board.

SHANGHAI ROSE ON THE SESSION LONDON FELL - the most-traded SHFE aluminium 2610 contract closed at RMB 24,100/t on 02-September, UP RMB 30 or +0.12%, holding above its 5-, 10-, 30- and 60-day moving averages, on volume of 163,674 lots and open interest down 6,267 lots as both sides took profit. With USD/CNY essentially unchanged at +0.02%, the divergence is real rather than an FX artefact. SMM attributes Chinese resilience to continued ingot destocking and the September peak season against hawkish Fed expectations. THIS PAGE ALSO CORRECTS ITS OWN NUMBER OPENLY: it had been carrying RMB 23,830, which traced to a 25-August print and was six sessions stale.

CHINESE INGOT SOCIAL INVENTORY FELL TO 850,000 TONNES AT END-AUGUST, in line with expectations, continuing a counter-seasonal destock that SMM expects to persist into September. This remains the single best physical counterweight on the page to a flatlining LME warehouse number, and it is the reason the demand-failure risk is held at a DOWN trend: the hard inventory series in the world's largest consuming market is pointing the right way even while sentiment surveys disagree with each other.

A RECOVERING SHFE/LME RATIO IS EXPECTED TO WEAKEN CHINESE EXPORT DEMAND AS ORDERS ON HAND ARE DIGESTED, per SMM's 02-September commentary. THIS IS THE BEARISH SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE OF THE SHANGHAI OUTPERFORMANCE REPORTED ABOVE and the two should be read together rather than separately: a Chinese market that holds up better than London makes Chinese metal less competitive abroad, which reduces the export flow that has been partially offsetting the Gulf shortfall. Chinese aluminium exports rose 18.7% year on year in the twelve months to July.

SECTION 232 IS RE-VERIFIED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND ANNEX I-A DERIVATIVES, 25% ON ANNEX I-B, effective 08-June-2026, with a 15% transitional rate for metal-intensive industrial and electrical-grid equipment through 31-December-2027. A Section 232 incentive programme effective 20-July-2026 additionally lets approved companies investing in US primary capacity import metal tied to expected output at HALF the applicable rate. At the 02-September cash official the tariff leg alone is $1,627.75/t, or 77.7% of the $2,094/t US Midwest duty-paid premium - the American premium is predominantly a policy variable, not a tightness variable.

KOREA'S RUSSIAN ALUMINIUM IMPORTS HIT A RECORD 483 kt AS SANCTIONS RISK DEEPENS, per AL Circle on 01-September. THIS MATTERS FOR THE INVENTORY ROW RATHER THAN FOR KOREA: LME warehouse stock is disproportionately Russian-origin, the LME has required attestations to warrant Russian metal in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026, and the EU import ban takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026. Metal being absorbed into non-sanctioning Asian consumption is metal that does not need to sit on an exchange, which is one mechanism by which a headline LME number can overstate genuinely available European supply.

FURTHER TANKER ATTACKS WERE REPORTED IN THE STRAIT ON 01/02-SEPTEMBER, including an Iranian strike on a Saudi tanker reported by the BBC to have killed two Filipino sailors, following two vessels struck on Monday night per the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre. THE PUBLIC SOURCES DISAGREE AND NEITHER IS SUPPRESSED HERE: open-source transit trackers describe the corridor as effectively closed, while the US Treasury Secretary stated on the record that 17 million barrels of crude crossed on Monday. What is not in dispute is that roughly 9% of world primary aluminium supply exits through the waterway and Gulf output was down 44% year on year in July.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 37.3% directional hit rate against a 69.2% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 1.08% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (102 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-06-05). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

status.name: Slovalco (Hydro / Penta JV, Slovakia)
status.status: RESTARTING - POTS FIRING UP AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE
status.impact: Bearish (European capacity returning, on a public and now-confirmed schedule)
status.update: NEW ROW ADDED THIS RUN ON A DATED PUBLIC REPORT AND IT MOVES A LINE THAT HAS SAT IN THE 'SCHEDULED' COLUMN FOR MONTHS INTO THE 'HAPPENING' COLUMN. AL Circle reported on 02-SEPTEMBER-2026 that Slovalco's smelters are firing up again after three years offline. The plant was curtailed in 2022 on European power costs and has been carried on this page as a scheduled Q4-2026 resumption of roughly 75 kt; a restart that has physically begun is a materially harder fact than a restart that is planned. THE COMMERCIAL SIGNIFICANCE IS DIRECTIONAL RATHER THAN LARGE: 75 kt is roughly a tenth of one per cent of world primary supply and will not move a balance on its own. WHAT IT DOES DO IS CONFIRM THE PATTERN THAT DOMINATES THE RISK PANEL - idled Western capacity is coming back because prices are high enough and margins wide enough to justify it, which is precisely the self-correcting mechanism that caps a price recovery. THE TENSION WORTH FLAGGING, AND IT IS UNRESOLVED: Slovalco is a gas-and-power-cost casualty restarting into a European gas market that just printed a multi-year high, with TTF up 3.00% on the session. A restart justified by metal prices can be un-justified by power prices, and this page will track whether the ramp holds rather than assuming it does.

status.name: US / Canada trade policy (Section 232)
status.status: 50% ON ARTICLES, 25% ON DERIVATIVES - VERIFIED; A US-CANADA CUT TO 25% IS REPORTED BUT NOT LAW
status.impact: Mixed (the largest single swing factor in the US delivered premium)
status.update: Verified against the primary source this run. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085 and effective 08-June-2026, holds the Annex I-A rate on aluminium articles at 50% and the Annex I-B derivative rate at 25%, with a 15% temporary subset now extended to agricultural equipment and residential HVAC, and aluminium lithographic plates newly brought into coverage. Annex I-C sets a 15% effective ceiling for a listed group including Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU member states, 10% where derivative aluminium content is entirely US-smelted and cast, and 25% on non-US content only for USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican goods with a 15% floor. THE PENDING CHANGE IS REPORTED, NOT ENACTED: a tentative framework to halve the Canadian rate to 25% was reported 19-August and drove an 8.2% single-session collapse in the September Midwest premium to 95.0 c/lb on 20-August. Commerce has separately offered a cut to 25% for producers that build or expand US facilities.

catalysts.text: US NON-FARM PAYROLLS FOR AUGUST - THE SINGLE HIGHEST-WEIGHT INPUT INTO THE 16-SEPTEMBER FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION, AND THE NEXT SCHEDULED EVENT ON THIS PAGE. The asymmetry is unusual and worth stating in advance: with a 25-basis-point HIKE already the majority-priced outcome at roughly 70%, a hot print largely confirms what is already in the curve, while a soft print has room to unwind a great deal of the bond selloff and the dollar strength that came with it. THAT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL TODAY because the dollar accounted for essentially the entire 0.17% aluminium decline on 02-September, so the currency is currently the dominant short-term driver of the flat price. Treat any pre-release estimate circulating in free reporting as an estimate.

WHETHER THE $2.00 BACKWARDATION WIDENS, HOLDS OR CLOSES - THE CONFIRMATION TEST FOR THE ONLY BULLISH SIGNAL THIS PAGE PRODUCED TODAY. The curve inverted on 02-September for the first time in twelve publishing sessions, with the prompt outperforming the forward for a second consecutive session and a cumulative $21.00 of front-end tightening. THE PRECEDENT IS DISCOURAGING AND IS STATED RATHER THAN OMITTED: the board printed exactly this +$2.00 inversion on 14-August and +$4.00 on 13-August, then spent twelve consecutive sessions back in contango. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS ONE DIFFERENT: a widening rather than static backwardation, held across several sessions, ALONGSIDE a stock draw an order of magnitude larger than the 500 tonnes recorded today. WHAT WORKS AGAINST IT: a $2.00 backwardation against a 4.8% funding rate pays nobody to carry metal, so the rational response to the current board is to deliver into the front, which resolves an inversion rather than sustaining it.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM NEGOTIATION, NOW PUBLIC AND RUNNING. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-$325/t for October-December shipments against the record Q3 settlement of $395/t, down 18-22%, citing positive Middle East restart progress and softer European premiums; buyers are targeting BELOW $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian shipments. Talks began the week of 24-August and Reuters reports they run through later this month. THE PENDING QUARTER IS SHOWN WITH A NULL VALUE AND A $290-325 SCENARIO RANGE, both bounds quoted from that single dated report rather than estimated. THE TWO FACTS THAT CANNOT BOTH BE FULLY PRICED, AND THE REASON THIS IS THE MOST COMMERCIALLY CONSEQUENTIAL ITEM ON THE PAGE: Japanese port stocks are at 201,000 t, the lowest since April 2010, and Gulf primary output was down 44% year on year in July.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - ROUGHLY A 70% MARKET-IMPLIED PROBABILITY OF A 25-BASIS-POINT HIKE, AND THE LARGEST SINGLE SCHEDULED RISK TO EVERY METAL ON THIS BOARD. The repricing has already driven global yields to multi-year highs, with the German 10-year at a fresh 15-year high and the 10-year JGB through 3%. THE TRANSMISSION IS NOW CURVE-SPECIFIC RATHER THAN GENERIC: with cash above three-month, holders are paid to lend metal to the prompt rather than to carry it, and $2.00 of backwardation against a 4.8% funding rate does not remotely cover the cost of holding. A hike widens that gap and pushes holders further toward delivering into the front - which is the specific mechanism that would close today's inversion without any change in the physical position.

FASTMARKETS INTERNATIONAL ALUMINIUM, 40TH EDITION - the industry's principal Q4 pricing-and-contracting gathering, with a published agenda covering emerging supply regions and Indonesia's expanding role, upstream bauxite and alumina risk, logistics, recycling and low-carbon aluminium. IT MATTERS BECAUSE OF ITS TIMING RATHER THAN ITS CONTENT: it sits directly on top of the now-live Q4 premium negotiation and immediately before the Federal Reserve decision, and 2027 annual-contract direction is conventionally set around it. Indonesia is on the agenda and is also the named reason Japanese buyers believe Asian balances are easing, which makes public read-outs from the event unusually relevant to the premium range on this page.

US MARAD ADVISORY 2026-006 ON THE RED SEA AND BAB EL MANDEB CORRIDOR REACHES ITS STATED EXPIRY - a scheduled decision point on whether the second impaired Middle East chokepoint is de-rated or extended. Bab el Mandeb transits remain down roughly 24% since the July Houthi blockade and carriers continue routing via the Cape, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. WHY IT SITS ON AN ALUMINIUM PAGE: with Hormuz the site of repeated physical strikes on tankers, there is currently no unimpaired routing between Gulf and Asian production and European consumption. No war-risk insurance reprice has been published since the 22-July mark of 7.5-10% of hull value, which should be read as a floor.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT, AND IT INTERACTS DIRECTLY WITH THE INVENTORY ROW. LME warehouse stock sits at 246,225 t and the available tonnage on that number is disproportionately Russian-origin; the LME has required attestations to warrant Russian metal in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026. KOREA'S RUSSIAN IMPORTS HITTING A RECORD 483 kt IS THE SAME STORY FROM THE OTHER SIDE: metal absorbed into non-sanctioning Asian consumption never needs to sit on an exchange. Headline LME stock therefore overstates metal deliverable into European consumption after year end, so a flat or slowly falling headline is a weaker comfort than it looks - which is the main reason this page reads it alongside Chinese social inventory rather than alone.

risks.text: TREND HELD AT UP AND REINFORCED BY TWO DATED ITEMS IN THE LAST 24 HOURS. FIRST, SLOVALCO'S SMELTERS ARE PHYSICALLY FIRING UP AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE per AL Circle on 02-September - roughly 75 kt moving from this page's 'scheduled' column into its 'happening' column, which is a materially harder fact than a plan. SECOND, AND MORE TELLING, THE PRODUCERS THEMSELVES CITED SUPPLY RELIEF AS THE REASON THEY CUT THEIR OWN PRICES: Reuters reports Q4-2026 Japanese premium offers of $310-325/t, down 18-22% on the $395 record, with the stated causes being a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer European premiums. When the sell side voluntarily opens 20% lower and names restart progress as the reason, that is the supply-relief risk being confirmed by the parties with the most information and the least incentive to confirm it. || SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD, AND THE CLOSED AUGUST MONTH IS NOW THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE ARGUMENT. The timetable is public and it advanced again this week: EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells - 315 of 1,262, up from roughly 18% a week ago - with all three potlines being worked and full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027; Century's Mt Holly is at FULL capacity for the first time since 2015, adding nearly 10% to total US primary output; Alcoa's San Ciprian restart completed in April and Portland has power secured to mid-2035; Hydro's Slovalco resumes 75 kt from Q4-2026 and Magnitude 7 Metals restarts 75 kt at Marston by end-2026; Tomago is underwritten to 2038 by a government package and a 10-year PPA. A CORRECTION MADE OPENLY THIS RUN REINFORCES THE POINT: this page had carried Alunorte at roughly 50% of capacity, but Hydro announced on 13-August that it was ramping the 6.3 Mtpa refinery back to FULL after ANP approved it as a gas self-importer. The largest alumina refinery outside China is not a live constraint. THE PRICE ALREADY KNOWS: aluminium's completed August monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, and its curve averaged a $1.60 contango against copper's $197.67 backwardation.

TREND CUT FROM UP TO FLAT - THE FLATLINE BROKE, BY THE SMALLEST MEANINGFUL AMOUNT THE EXCHANGE REPORTS, AND THAT IS WORTH EXACTLY WHAT IT IS WORTH AND NO MORE. Warehouse stock fell 500 t to 246,225 t on 02-September after printing 246,725 t for three consecutive sessions and moving 200 t across the thirteen sessions from 17-August; today's single move exceeds that whole thirteen-session total. IT IS ALSO 0.20% OF THE STOCK AND ROUGHLY TWO HOURS OF WORLD PRIMARY OUTPUT, and lead - a metal with no supply story whatsoever - drew 5,075 t on the same board, ten times as much. THE TREND IS SET TO FLAT RATHER THAN DOWN DELIBERATELY: the risk that the draw has stopped is no longer worsening, because it demonstrably resumed, but a single 500-tonne session is not enough evidence to call it improving. What makes it worth anything at all is that it coincided with the curve inverting - the first session in this cycle on which inventory and structure pointed the same way at the same time. || THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED, AND THE COMPLETED MONTH NOW SHOWS EXACTLY WHEN IT STOPPED. LME aluminium warehouse stock fell from 262,650 t on 03-August to 246,925 t on 17-August and then moved 200 TONNES ACROSS THE FINAL NINE SESSIONS OF THE MONTH, closing at 246,725 t. The draw did not decelerate gradually - it halted, and it halted three weeks before the month ended. August's average stock of 251,215 t against July's 282,350 t is an 11.0% monthly decline, which is real but ranks THIRD of five: copper -22.6%, zinc -14.3%, aluminium -11.0%, nickel -2.2%, lead +8.9%. A DEFICIT NARRATIVE REQUIRES INVENTORY TO KEEP FALLING; this one has flatlined at a level that is historically low but no longer directional, while the metal sitting on it is disproportionately Russian-origin ahead of a 31-December-2026 EU import ban. THE ONE GENUINE COUNTERWEIGHT IS CHINESE AND IT IS CONSTRUCTIVE: ingot social inventory fell to 837,000 t on 31-August, down 15,000 t on the prior Thursday and 23,000 t on the prior Monday, for a cumulative August destock of 106,000 t and 278,000 t off the early-July peak - counter-seasonal, and SMM expects it to continue through the first half of September.

TREND RAISED BACK FROM DOWN TO UP AFTER ONE SESSION, AND THE REVERSAL IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN QUIETLY MADE. This risk is the risk that the market STOPS PAYING for the Gulf disruption, not the risk of the disruption itself. It was cut to DOWN yesterday because aluminium led the entire LME board on 01-September while copper and nickel fell on the same hostile macro. ON 02-SEPTEMBER THAT LEADERSHIP DID NOT REPEAT: aluminium finished THIRD OF FIVE at -0.17%, behind nickel at +1.10%, while the underlying story got WORSE rather than better - further tanker attacks were reported in the Strait on 01/02-September including an Iranian strike on a Saudi tanker reported to have killed two Filipino sailors, Brent rose a fourth consecutive session to $95.117 and European gas rose 3.00% to a 2023 high. THE ENERGY COMPLEX KEPT PAYING AND THE METAL DID NOT. A risk premium that decays while its cause persists is a positioning phenomenon, and positioning unwinds faster than shortages do - which is precisely the risk this row exists to track. || GULF SUPPLY DISRUPTION IS REAL AND PARTLY UNDATED - AND ON 01-SEPTEMBER THE MARKET STARTED PAYING FOR IT AGAIN. THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN THIS RUN, MEANING THE RISK THAT THE DISRUPTION STORY GOES UNPAID IS RECEDING RATHER THAN THE DISRUPTION ITSELF BEING RESOLVED. The evidence is one dated session and it is unusually clean: aluminium cash rose 1.21% to $3,261.00 and led the entire LME board while copper fell 0.96% and nickel 2.97% on the SAME session and the SAME hostile macro, and the $19.00 contango closed to zero. When a shared macro pushes four metals down and one up, the one going up is being bid for something the others do not have. THE TRIGGER WAS DATED AND PHYSICAL: two oil tankers, one Saudi and one South Korean, were struck by projectiles inside the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night per the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre; the US struck Iranian targets around the Strait in retaliation for attempted mine-laying; Iran responded against US bases and fired missiles toward Jordan; Brent rose a third consecutive session above $95. THE PHYSICAL POSITION UNDERNEATH HAS NOT MOVED IN MONTHS: Qatalum at roughly 60% of 648 kt on reduced gas with NO published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba's reduction Lines 1-3 idle since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with a stated intention to REPLACE rather than restart. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS DATED TOO AND IS NOT SUPPRESSED: the US Treasury Secretary stated that 17 million barrels of crude crossed Hormuz on Monday, which is not the throughput of a closed strait. What is being priced is disruption probability, not realised disruption - and probability premia unwind faster than shortages do.

TREND HELD AT DOWN, AND THE HARD INVENTORY SERIES REMAINS THE REASON. Chinese ingot social inventory finished August at 850,000 t, in line with expectations, on a counter-seasonal destock SMM expects to continue into September; SHFE aluminium 2610 closed HIGHER on 02-September at RMB 24,100/t on a session London closed lower, with USD/CNY essentially unchanged so the divergence is not an FX artefact. SMM credits the September peak season explicitly. THE HONEST BEARISH OFFSET INSIDE THE SAME SOURCE IS NOT SUPPRESSED: SMM also notes the recovering SHFE/LME ratio is expected to WEAKEN Chinese export demand as orders on hand are digested, which reduces the export flow that has been partially offsetting the Gulf shortfall. Chinese exports rose 18.7% year on year in the twelve months to July, so that flow is large enough for its reduction to matter. || PHYSICAL DEMAND FAILS TO SHOW UP FOR THE PEAK SEASON, AND CHINA'S OWN SURVEYS NOW DISAGREE ABOUT WHETHER IT IS COMING. TREND HELD AT DOWN, BECAUSE THE HARD INVENTORY DATA IS THE ONE SERIES POINTING THE RIGHT WAY. The official NBS manufacturing PMI printed 49.8 for August, up from 49.2 but in contraction for a second month, with employment at 48.7 and non-manufacturing at 49.0; the private RatingDog index printed 51.5 against 50.9 expected, a substantial beat. The official panel skews to large state heavy industry and the private one to smaller exporters, and they have diverged repeatedly through 2026, so the August China demand signal is UNRESOLVED rather than positive. China's aluminium PROCESSING composite PMI is unambiguous, though, at 48.7% - up slightly but still contracting, with September expected to return to expansion. PV frame operating rates are strong on POLICY-DRIVEN advance stockpiling ahead of an expected US Section 232 solar rule rather than on end demand, with forward oversupply pressure behind it. Against all of that, ingot social inventory keeps falling counter-seasonally and European foil deliveries rose 5.8% quarter on quarter in Q2. The physical draw is the better evidence and it is why this trend stays down.

HELD AT UP AND THE MECHANISM SHARPENED TODAY IN A WAY THAT IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN ATMOSPHERIC. The global bond selloff extended - US 10-year 4.817%, UK 5.283%, the 10-year JGB through 3% at 3.018%, Australia 5.225%, and the GERMAN 10-YEAR AT 3.3884%, FLAGGED AS A FRESH 15-YEAR HIGH - with roughly a 70% probability of a 25-basis-point US rate HIKE priced for 16-September. WHY IT BITES HARDER NOW THAT THE CURVE HAS INVERTED: a backwardation means holders are PAID to lend metal to the prompt rather than paying to carry it, and $2.00 of backwardation against a 4.8% funding rate does not come close to compensating a carry. Rising funding costs and an inverted curve push the rational holder the SAME way - toward delivering metal into the front. That is the mechanism by which a backwardation resolves itself rather than persisting, and it is why today's curve signal should not be extrapolated. || MACRO AND RATES OVERWHELM THE MICRO - HELD AT UP AND NOW THE SINGLE LARGEST BEARISH FORCE ON THIS PAGE, WITH A DATED SCHEDULED EVENT ATTACHED TO IT. Money markets are pricing roughly a 70% PROBABILITY OF A 25 BASIS-POINT US RATE HIKE ON 16-SEPTEMBER, after the Federal Reserve chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut on 28-August and his statement that inflation is not slowing meaningfully; ECB officials are separately reported to be leaning toward a September hike. THE GLOBAL BOND SELLOFF HAS DRIVEN YIELDS TO THEIR HIGHEST SINCE 2008: US 10-year 4.808%, UK 5.225%, the 10-year JGB THROUGH 3% at 3.014%, the Australian 10-year at 5.196% and a fresh 15-YEAR HIGH, the German 10-year 3.339%, the Canadian 10-year at a 27-month high. Gold has erased its entire 2026 gain and equity indices fell worldwide - Nikkei -2.89%, ASX 200 -1.81%, Shanghai -0.82%. EVERY TRANSMISSION CHANNEL RUNS THE WRONG WAY FOR AN INDUSTRIAL METAL: higher real rates raise the cost of financing physical inventory, which is the mechanism that turns a flat or contangoed curve into forced selling rather than into profitable storage; they compress the demand outlook that every deficit forecast on this page depends on; and a firmer dollar - DXY 99.798, and a 0.46% stronger dollar between the 28-August and 01-September LME fixings - mechanically lowers a dollar-denominated price. THE ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS RISK READ SLIGHTLY DIFFERENTLY TODAY: aluminium rose 1.21% straight into all of it, which says the metal-specific bid was strong enough to overwhelm the macro for one session. One session.

HELD AT UP WITH ONE NEW DATED POINT AND ONE HONEST ADMISSION. THE NEW POINT IS ENERGY: European gas TTF rose 3.00% to a 2023 high on Strait-related supply news, with UK gas doing the same and Brent up a fourth session at $95.117. Gas-indexed European power is the marginal high-cost tonne in the Western system, so this is simultaneously a cost input and a curtailment risk on exactly the restart pipeline listed in the first risk row - Slovalco is a 2022 power-cost casualty restarting into a multi-year gas high. THE ADMISSION IS THAT THE REST OF THE BASKET HAD NO NEW MARKS: prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petcoke are on monthly settlement cycles publishing around the 17th-18th, and no newer free dated SMM fluoride-salt, silicon or magnesium print was retrievable this morning. A silicon futures quote WAS available and was deliberately not appended because it is a different basis from the row's SMM spot series. THE COUNTERWEIGHT REMAINS DECISIVE: SMM puts China's weighted all-in cost DOWN 0.7% month on month with average margins of RMB 7,890/t, up 87.7% year on year, and 100% of operating capacity profitable. Cost inflation here is a margin risk, not a supply-side price support. || INPUT-COST INFLATION THROUGH FREIGHT, CARBON AND BAUXITE - HELD AT UP, WITH TWO NEW DATED POINTS THIS RUN. The carbon chain turned: a large Shandong smelter set its SEPTEMBER prebaked anode tender at RMB 5,730/t, UP RMB 100 month on month, ending four months of drift; and PetroChina raised low-sulphur petroleum coke list prices at ALL FIVE of its North-East China refineries effective 00:00 on 01-September. SMM's cost note adds that fluoride salts rose through August with further increases expected in September, and that coal gains will push September power tariffs moderately higher. Freight is the largest single inflation: the Baltic Dry Index closed at 3,186 on 28-August, its seventh consecutive gain and highest since 02-June, up 21.05% on the month and 57.33% on the year, Capesize-led - which is the ore-and-bauxite end. Imported bauxite CIF is the driver SMM names behind rising Chinese alumina costs. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, AND IT IS LARGE: SMM puts China's weighted all-in production cost DOWN 0.7% month on month and 3.4% year on year in August, with an average smelter margin of RMB 7,890/t - up 87.7% year on year - and 100% of operating capacity profitable. A RMB 100/t anode increase against a RMB 7,890/t margin is a rounding item, which is precisely why cost inflation is a margin risk and not a supply-side price support.

TREND FLIPPED FROM DOWN TO UP AND THE ROW IS RE-FRAMED, BECAUSE THE PREVIOUS FRAMING WAS CONFUSING. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT ALUMINA LOOSENS FASTER THAN METAL AND REMOVES THE COST-SIDE CONSTRAINT ON EVERYONE'S OUTPUT - AND THAT RISK IS NOW ACTIVELY MATERIALISING, so its trend is UP and its impact is raised to High. SMM's 02-SEPTEMBER read is unusually explicit: strong supply against weak demand, Chinese domestic production recovering month on month, Guangxi steadily ramping with new capacity about to be released and Shanxi resuming this month, the ex-China supply-mismatch logic that supported high prices weakening with prices pulling back, July net imports down month on month, PORT INVENTORIES CLIMBED TO HISTORICAL HIGHS, plant inventories rising with output - and an explicit conclusion that supply pressure is only increasing, demand shows no bright spots, prices still have downside room and the build will continue. ADD THE TWO REFINERY RESTORATIONS: Alunorte ramping back to full after ANP approved it as a gas self-importer, and EGA's Al Taweelah refinery at roughly 50% and rising with EGA stating its smelter recovery is not gated on it. THE CONSEQUENCE IS BEARISH FOR METAL EVEN THOUGH IT IS BULLISH FOR SMELTERS, and that distinction is the whole point of the row: with margins up 87.7% year on year and the alumina input cheapening, there is no cost mechanism anywhere in the world forcing a curtailment. Every tonne that can run, runs. || ALUMINA LOOSENS FASTER THAN METAL AND THE SMELTER MARGIN STOPS BEING A CONSTRAINT ON ANYONE'S OUTPUT - TREND SET TO DOWN THIS RUN, MEANING THE RISK OF AN ALUMINA-DRIVEN COST SQUEEZE IS FALLING RATHER THAN THE RISK ITSELF BEING BENIGN. The SMM Alumina Index averaged RMB 2,695/t across the 26-July to 25-August window, DOWN 1.8% month on month; 30,000 t traded at $379/mt FOB Indonesia on 31-August for October shipment; Hydro's Alunorte is ramping back to full after its August gas interruption rather than sitting at 50%; EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is at roughly 50% and rising. THE CONSEQUENCE IS BEARISH FOR METAL EVEN THOUGH IT IS BULLISH FOR SMELTERS, and the distinction is the point: with 100% of Chinese operating capacity profitable and margins up 87.7% year on year, there is no cost-side mechanism anywhere in the world forcing a curtailment. Every tonne that can run, runs. China's domestic alumina at RMB 2,600-2,700 against a national weighted full cost of RMB 2,718/t is the one floor in the system, and it is a floor under alumina, not under aluminium.

HELD AT UP, WITH THE RATE RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN AND ONE PROVISION ADDED THAT THIS PAGE HAD NOT PREVIOUSLY CARRIED. Section 232 is confirmed at 50% on aluminium articles and Annex I-A derivatives and 25% on Annex I-B derivatives, effective 08-June-2026, with a 15% transitional rate for metal-intensive industrial and electrical-grid equipment running through 31-December-2027. THE ADDITION IS A SECTION 232 INCENTIVE PROGRAMME EFFECTIVE 20-JULY-2026 under which approved companies investing in US primary aluminium capacity may import primary metal tied to expected output at HALF the applicable rate - a carve-out that creates a second, lower effective tariff for a subset of importers and therefore a second, lower effective premium for them. At the 02-September cash official of $3,255.50 the headline tariff leg is $1,627.75/t, or 77.7% of the $2,094/t US Midwest duty-paid premium. || US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE DELIVERED PREMIUM MORE THAN THE PHYSICAL MARKET DOES, AND THE PRICED-IN RELIEF HAS NOT BEEN ENACTED. HELD AT UP. Section 232 is verified at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives under Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, 91 FR 34085. At the 28-August cash official of $3,222.00 that is $1,611/t of pure duty, which is roughly 77% of a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094/t - the American premium is predominantly a policy variable, not a tightness variable. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
